concerns.concern: The XRD evidence does not show that the intermediate phase is monoclinic P2₁/c (B2₁/a) rather than orthorhombic Bmab. The superlattice reflections at q = (½,½,0) and the 2-fold superstructure are common to both space groups.
concerns.quote: The superlattice reflections at q = (½,½,0) of I4/mmm (Fig. 2b) and the "2-fold superstructure" are common to both Bmab and P2₁/c

concerns.concern: The main argument against Li et al. rests on 300 K data near 10.5 GPa. At that temperature the monoclinic angle β is essentially 90°, so there is no metric evidence for monoclinic symmetry.
concerns.quote: The text concedes the monoclinic distortion is "negligible" at 300 K (Fig. 4b, β ≈ 90.0–90.05°), yet the 300 K data near 10.5 GPa are the main argument

concerns.concern: The weak centering-violating reflections are attributed to twin domains, and Li et al. saw very similar patterns. The authors should list the reflections allowed in B2₁/a but extinct in Bmab, and show with the refined twin model that their intensities cannot come from overlap of other domains' reflections.
concerns.quote: The distinction therefore rests on interpretation and on the refinement comparison in Table S4.

concerns.concern: Lower R-values for the lower-symmetry model are not convincing, because extra coordinates and twin fractions almost always lower R. The authors should report parameter counts, data/parameter ratio, completeness and R_int, and apply a Hamilton R-ratio test.
concerns.quote: With four pseudo-merohedral domains, a lower-symmetry model with more free coordinates and twin fractions will almost always lower R.

concerns.concern: The Bmab versus P2₁/c model comparison is shown only at 10.5 GPa and 300 K. It should be repeated at other pressures and at 80 K and 20 K, where the monoclinic distortion is resolvable. Without this, the claim of 'no trace' of Bmab is unsupported.
concerns.quote: show the comparison at several pressures and temperatures (especially 80/20 K, where β − 90° ≈ 0.3–0.5° is resolvable), not only at 10.5 GPa/300 K.

concerns.concern: An unconstrained DFT relaxation inside P2₁/c only tests the stability of the starting structure, and the Methods admit the outcome depends on the starting point and force threshold. Constrained-symmetry enthalpy curves ΔH(P) for I4/mmm, Fmmm, Bmab and P2₁/c are needed, and ideally phonon calculations.
concerns.quote: A symmetry-unconstrained relaxation inside P2₁/c tests the stability of the structure it starts from.

concerns.concern: The DFT convergence is too coarse for the small enthalpy differences at stake. Energies are converged only to 1 mHa (≈27 meV), the 2×4×4 k-mesh is coarse for this metal, and the smearing scheme and width are not given.
concerns.quote: Total energies are converged only to 1 mHa (≈27 meV per cell). The Bmab/P2₁/c enthalpy differences are probably well below this.

concerns.concern: The DFT work ignores spin polarization, although the ambient ground state has an SDW, and it ignores functional dependence. Tilt instabilities are sensitive to PBE versus PBEsol/LDA, so at least the critical pressure should be recomputed with PBEsol.
concerns.quote: Spin polarization (the ambient ground state has an SDW) and functional dependence are not discussed.

concerns.concern: The paper is not internally consistent: on p. 8 the transition is called weakly first-order and, a few lines later, continuous.
concerns.quote: p. 8 calls the transition "a weak first-order phase transition" (jump in β) and, a few lines later, "continuous".

concerns.concern: A direct I4/mmm → P2₁/c transition may require two distinct X-point irreps, which would make it generically first-order or fine-tuned. A symmetry-mode decomposition (e.g., ISODISTORT) is needed to identify the active irreps, their amplitudes and the expected couplings.
concerns.quote: If the P2₁/c tilt pattern in this n = 3 compound requires two distinct irreps at the X point... a direct transition is generically first-order or requires fine-tuning.

concerns.concern: The reported (P_c − P)^½ scaling of β − 90° is symmetry-suspicious. A Γ-point shear strain cannot couple linearly to an X-point tilt amplitude, so a higher power would be expected.
concerns.quote: a (P_c − P)^½ scaling for it (Fig. 5, p. 11) is symmetry-suspicious; a product-of-order-parameters coupling would give a higher power.

concerns.concern: The ±0.04 GPa uncertainty on the critical pressure is not meaningful. It comes from fitting only the three points nearest P_c with fixed exponents.
concerns.quote: It comes from fitting the three points nearest P_c with fixed exponents, which constrains little.

concerns.concern: Hysteresis between compression and decompression, and phase coexistence near the boundary, are not tested. These tests are needed to assess the claimed first-order character.
concerns.quote: test for hysteresis on compression versus decompression and for phase coexistence near the boundary.

concerns.concern: The Raman selection rules do not hold, because the polarizations are not along crystal axes in the bc plane, so both channels mix A_g and B_g. The '31 modes > 24 A_g' argument therefore fails, and the total of 51 may count modes twice.
concerns.quote: The "31 modes in parallel > 24 A_g" argument therefore fails, and the total of 51 counts a mode twice if it appears in both channels.

concerns.concern: The remaining excess over P2₁/c is only three modes (51 vs 48). That margin is within what leakage, two-phonon features, magnetic excitations, side phases or RP intergrowths could produce.
concerns.quote: The remaining margin over P2₁/c (51 vs 48) is three modes, which is within the range of

concerns.concern: Zone folding by an incommensurate density wave can create new Raman lines without lowering the point group. Counting modes against Pc/P2₁ is therefore not meaningful unless the authors check whether the new modes match folded dispersions at the DW wavevector.
concerns.quote: This alone produces new Raman lines without any lowering of the point group. Counting against 3D space groups Pc/P2₁ is then not meaningful.

concerns.concern: For the Raman claim, the crystal axes and twin state of the Raman sample are not determined. Angle-resolved polarized Raman and a de-duplicated mode table with fit uncertainties are needed.
concerns.quote: determine the in-plane crystal axes of the Raman crystal (Laue or XRD) and its twin state;

concerns.concern: Any claim of inversion-symmetry breaking needs a direct test, such as SHG or a check of IR/Raman mutual exclusion.
concerns.quote: if inversion breaking is to be claimed, add a direct test, such as SHG or IR/Raman coincidence (breakdown of mutual exclusion).

concerns.concern: The Raman conclusion should be narrowed to new excitations below T_DW, consistent with DW-induced folding and/or symmetry lowering.
concerns.quote: the conclusion should be narrowed to "new Raman-active excitations below T_DW, consistent with DW-induced folding and/or symmetry lowering".

concerns.concern: The paper claims both that the density wave causes no discernible structural distortion and that a third structural phase is associated with it. These statements need to be reconciled.
concerns.quote: the paper simultaneously asserts "no discernible structural distortions associated with DW ordering" (Abstract) and "a third structural phase associated with the DW".

concerns.concern: The claim that superconductivity emerges only in the tetragonal phase is not tested, since there are no transport or susceptibility data under pressure. Either R(T)/χ(T) data on the same batch are needed, or the claim should be rephrased as consistency with the literature.
concerns.quote: This affirms that superconductivity emerges only once the system is restored to the tetragonal phase" is not tested.

concerns.concern: The text infers on p. 4 that superconductivity emerges within tetragonal symmetry from the absence of Bmab. These are logically separate statements.
concerns.quote: "superconductivity emerges within the tetragonal symmetry" is inferred from the absence of Bmab. These are logically separate statements.

concerns.concern: The phase boundary is sparsely sampled, with no data between 0 and 10 GPa above room temperature. The linear suppression from 1030 K is therefore an unconstrained interpolation that should be supported with more points or labelled a conjecture.
concerns.quote: Nothing lies between 0 and 10 GPa above room temperature, so "progressively suppressed from 1030 K" and the dashed linear boundary are unconstrained

concerns.concern: The criterion and uncertainty for the transition temperature/pressure are not stated. Fig. 2a already shows elongation at 9 GPa while the text places the onset at 10.5 GPa; integrated superlattice intensity versus pressure would give a quantitative transition point.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2a already shows elongation at 9 GPa/300 K, while the text places the onset at 10.5 GPa.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature transition pressure of 10.5 GPa should be reconciled with the ~15 GPa quoted from the literature, considering pressure medium, oxygen stoichiometry and detection criterion.
concerns.quote: The 10.5 GPa room-temperature value should be reconciled with the ~15 GPa quoted in the Introduction from [19–22].

concerns.concern: The null result for density-wave satellites has no stated sensitivity. An upper bound relative to main reflections, a comparison with Zhang et al., and reciprocal-space maps (including a difference map) at 20 K and 150 K are needed.
concerns.quote: An upper bound on satellite intensity relative to main reflections should be given and compared with the intensities reported by Zhang et al. [25].

concerns.concern: Nothing shows that these flux-grown crystals have a density wave at all; there are no resistivity, susceptibility or heat-capacity data establishing T_DW. Oxygen stoichiometry is known to control the DW.
concerns.quote: The paper shows no resistivity, susceptibility or heat-capacity data establishing T_DW ≈ 130 K in these flux-grown crystals.

concerns.concern: The ambient-pressure DESY data should be checked for the known lattice-parameter anomaly (negative thermal expansion of b) across T_DW.
concerns.quote: The DESY ambient-pressure data should be used to check for the lattice-parameter anomaly (negative thermal expansion of b) reported in [36–38] across T_DW.

concerns.concern: Oxygen content is not quantified; EPMA is reported to confirm only the La:Ni ratio, even though an oxygen standard was used.
concerns.quote: Oxygen content is not quantified. EPMA is said to confirm only La:Ni = 4:3, although an oxygen standard was used.

concerns.concern: The batch contains NiO and La₂NiO₄. It is not stated whether the SXRD and Raman crystals were screened for these or for intergrowths of other n phases.
concerns.quote: The authors should state whether the crystals used for SXRD and Raman were screened for intergrowths of other n phases.

concerns.concern: The paper does not state how many crystals were measured in the DAC, whether the 300/80/20 K series used the same crystal, or whether the Raman crystal came from the same batch.
concerns.quote: It is not stated how many crystals were measured in the DAC, whether the 300, 80 and 20 K series used the same crystal

concerns.concern: The claim that the transition is impervious to crystal-growth variations is drawn from flux crystals only. It should be restated as a comparison with the literature.
concerns.quote: The paper's claim that the transition is "impervious to variations in the crystal growth process" is drawn from flux crystals only

concerns.concern: The SI lacks per-pressure refinement statistics for the DAC data: completeness, number of unique reflections, data/parameter ratio, twin fractions and R values.
concerns.quote: The SI should give completeness, number of unique reflections, data/parameter ratio, twin fractions and R values for each pressure point.

concerns.concern: The β values at 80 K and 20 K scatter by ~0.2–0.3° between points, yet the caption says error bars are smaller than the symbols. The stated uncertainties are unrealistic.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b at 80 K and 20 K shows point-to-point scatter of β of ~0.2–0.3°, while the caption states that "error bars are smaller than the symbols".

concerns.concern: The 80 K tilt data stop at ~9.5 GPa although the phase stays monoclinic to ~13 GPa. The missing points are needed for the claimed comparison with DFT near the critical pressure.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3c 80 K tilt data stop at ~9.5 GPa although the phase is monoclinic to ~13 GPa.

concerns.concern: The ~18% stiffening of the bulk modulus K₀ from 300 K to 80/20 K is unusually large and may reflect K′–K₀ correlation. The EOS order, whether K′ was fixed, and whether data across the transition were pooled should be stated.
concerns.quote: K₀ changes from 155(4) GPa at 300 K to 182–185 GPa at 80/20 K. This ~18% stiffening is unusually large and may reflect K′–K₀ correlation.

concerns.concern: The low-temperature temperature correction for ruby pressure calibration is not described. Nor is it stated whether pressure was measured at the measurement temperature after cooling.
concerns.quote: Ruby calibration (IPPS-Ruby2020) needs a temperature correction below room temperature. Please state how it was applied

concerns.concern: It is not explained how the 26 K Raman sample temperature, including laser heating, was determined.
concerns.quote: For Raman, explain how the 26 K sample temperature including laser heating was determined (e.g., Stokes/anti-Stokes ratio).

concerns.concern: It is unclear how the temperature range '120–150 K' relates to T_DW.
concerns.quote: Explain how the range "120–150 K" relates to T_DW.

concerns.concern: The ambient β deviation from powder XRD (0.1–0.2°) appears larger than the low-pressure 300 K SXRD values (~0.05°) and should be reconciled.
concerns.quote: The ambient β deviation from PXRD (0.1–0.2°, Fig. S1) appears larger than the 300 K low-pressure SXRD values in Fig. 4b (~0.05°).

concerns.concern: T_DW is quoted inconsistently as 135 K, 130 K and ~120 K. A single value with a stated criterion should be used.
concerns.quote: T_DW is given as 135 K (Abstract), 130 K and ~120 K at different places.

concerns.concern: The mode counts for P2₁/Pc include acoustic modes, while the other space groups are counted differently. Counting should be consistent across space groups.
concerns.quote: the counts for P2₁/Pc (51A + 51B) include acoustic modes. The Raman-active optical counts are 50A + 49B for P2₁

concerns.concern: The Methods description of the P2₁/c cell, with the stacking axis along a and doubled, is confusing given the B2₁/a cell. The explicit cell should be given.
concerns.quote: "within the P2₁/c setting the RP stacking axis is oriented along a and is doubled" is confusing given the B2₁/a cell.

concerns.concern: The DFT threshold for stresses is quoted in force units (Ha/Bohr); stresses need their own units.
concerns.quote: The force threshold is quoted for both forces and stresses in Ha/Bohr; stresses need their own units.

concerns.concern: Fig. 5's triple y-axis layout, with the β axis placed at P_c, is hard to read. Separate panels with explicit DFT error bars are suggested.
concerns.quote: the triple y-axis arrangement, with the β axis placed at P_c, is hard to read. Consider separate panels and show the DFT error bars explicitly.

concerns.concern: There are typos and inconsistencies: an author-name mismatch, misspellings, P_c vs Pc in Table I, and inconsistent capitalization of chemical formulas in the references.
concerns.quote: "Gaston Gabarino" in the author list vs "G. Garbarino" in Ref. [60]; "propoposal", "PsuedoDojo", "monotonously"
